summary: Join our training course on sustainable financing models for social protection. Learn strategies to enhance social welfare and drive meaningful impact.
lede: Sustainable financing models for social protection help turn funding from a high-level commitment into a practical discipline. This course shows you how to map financing sources, assess fiscal space, cost programs, evaluate revenue options, and combine domestic and external resources. You will learn to weigh coverage, adequacy, and sustainability when planning cash transfers, social insurance, subsidies, and safety nets. Through realistic scenarios, tools, and templates, you will build the skills to prioritize, negotiate, and justify financing decisions within real budget and political environments.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals tasked with engaging in the financing, budgeting, or expansion of social protection systems. This course is designed for: Social protection practitioners and program managers in government ministries. Policy analysts and advisors in ministries of finance, planning, or social development. NGO and civil society leaders managing social protection and safety net programs. Social insurance fund managers and pension administrators. Development partner staff involved in funding, co-financing, or advising social protection. Budget, planning, and public finance officers supporting social sector allocations. Monitoring and evaluation specialists who link program performance to financing decisions. Social policy consultants and technical advisors working on reforms or scale-up. Donor-funded project managers planning exit strategies and domestic resource mobilization. Anyone who must justify, negotiate, or design financing for social protection schemes.
modules: Foundations of Social Protection and Sustainable Financing
Mapping the Social Protection Financing Landscape
Comparing Financing Models for Social Protection
Public Financial Management (PFM) for Social Protection
Leveraging Development Partners and Managing Transitions
Equity, Targeting, and Political Economy of Financing Choices
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of social protection systems and basic public finance principles. Experience in social policy, budgeting, or program management is recommended.
